metadata.case_name: LEE BON YET WILLIAM v. UNCLE RESTAURANT MANAGEMENT LTD

plaintiff.occupation_after: part-time waiter at a restaurant called On the Rock (Toronto)

injuries.description: spinal fractures to his left tibia and fibula
source: Diagnosis revealed that the plaintiff had suffered spinal fractures to his left tibia and fibula.
An external fixation device was fixed on his left leg on 26 September 2000.

manifestations.description: pain over his left lower leg
episodes of stabbing pain occasionally, especially at night and during bad weather, which pain might wake him up
cannot run or jump and has to take extra care when climbing stairs and walking on slopes
can walk and stoop; can also squat but not for a prolonged period because of his left leg's weakness
10 circular scars on the left lower leg which resulted from the insertion of the external fixator
tenderness on percussion on the medial aspect of his left shin at the distal one-third of the left tibia
left thigh girth 1 cm less than right and left calf girth 1.5 cm less than right indicating some slight muscle wasting of the left leg
movement of the ankle joint relatively limited because of stiffness
According to the AMA Guide for Evaluation of Permanent Impairment (5th edition), the plaintiff had 3 per cent total body impairment

treatments_received: external fixation surgery (external fixation device fixed on his left leg on 26 September 2000)
discharged and sent to the Maclehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre on 5 October 2000 for rehabilitation
physiotherapy as an in-patient in the Maclehose Centre for ten and a half months
physiotherapy as an outpatient for a further one and a half months

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He could not run or jump and had to take extra care when climbing stairs and walking on slopes.
Residual deformity and scarring of the left lower leg (including 10 circular scars) and slight muscle wasting.
Reduced efficiency at work and reduced earning capacity resulting from the left leg injury.
